title: What if the jumps in a sequence keep growing?
description: The jumps between terms are three, four, five and six, each one bigger than the one before. The video uses the next jump to find the next term, and Keeko's doubt, that the jump is always the same, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the jumps themselves follow a pattern, use that pattern to find the next jump. Watch for students who assume every sequence adds the same number each time.

video_script.why: The child sees that the jumps can change by a rule of their own, and uses the next jump to find the next term.
video_script.substitution: When the jumps grow by one each time, the next jump is one more than the last jump.
video_script.anchor: a row of five number cards 2, 5, 9, 14, 20 with curved arrows between them that grow a little bigger each time
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the jump is always three, because the first jump is three. Fourteen plus three is seventeen, but the list says twenty, so the jump is not fixed and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The next term is twenty seven

final_answer.spoken: the next term is twenty seven

maths_rules: the jumps grow by 1 each time, so the next jump is 7
slip: a sequence need not add the same number each time
video_script.design: One idea: the jumps can follow a rule of their own. Assumes finding a jump. Wrong idea: the jump is always the same. The cards stay on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; five number cards in a row: 2, 5, 9, 14, 20

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.cards: the five number cards appear one by one
marks.ask: a question mark card appears after the last number

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a list of numbers.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>It begins two, five, nine, fourteen, twenty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which number comes next in this list?

beats.on_screen: the cards hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a short walk along the number line from 2 to 5, with the jump drawn as an arrow and labelled jump

marks.arrow: an arrow from two to five is drawn and labelled jump
marks.count: the arrow is measured against the number line

narration: <bookmark mark='arrow'/>The jump from one term to the next tells us how far we have moved.
<bookmark mark='count'/>To find a jump, we take the smaller term away from the bigger one.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the terms two, five, nine, fourteen and twenty.

marks.find: the words the next term are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the next term.

marks.jumps: an arrow between the first three terms is labelled with its jump
marks.more: the last two arrows are labelled with their jumps

narration: <bookmark mark='jumps'/>Step one, find each jump. Five is three more than two, and nine is four more than five.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Fourteen is five more than nine, and twenty is six more than fourteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, the jumps are 3, 4, 5, 6, each one bigger by 1, so the next jump is 7

marks.grow: the jumps 3, 4, 5, 6 are lined up with a plus 1 between each pair, then 7 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='grow'/>Step two, look at the jumps themselves. They are three, four, five and six, and each is one bigger than the one before. The next jump is seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, add the next jump to the last term: 20 + 7 = 27

marks.next: a new card appears after twenty with 27 on it

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step three, add the next jump to the last term. Twenty plus seven is twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The next term is twenty seven, because the jump grew by one again.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble over the first arrow; 14 + 3 = 17 is written beside the card 20 with a cross; the bubble is struck through and the four arrows grow in size

marks.doubt: the bubble appears over the first arrow
marks.test: 14 + 3 = 17 is written beside the card 20, with a cross
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the four arrows are shown growing

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the jump is always three, because the first jump is three.
<bookmark mark='test'/>But fourteen plus three is seventeen, and the list says twenty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The jumps are not fixed, so we must check every one of them.
